items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: Oh, like old man Adolph Alexander, that's Tatan, old man, we would call him Tatan, you know.

ctx.x: You couldn't call them a brass band.

No, but I mean, who were some of the great baritone players of the brass band? Oh, like old man Adolph Alexander, that's Tatan, old man, we would call him Tatan, you know. And we had Georgia Hooker across the river and you had Vic Gaspar, you had Eddie Ackage, you had one of them was good baritone, good baritone players they call that. Called Vic Gaspar, he was good.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: I must have written the name after my father's friend, Adolph Alexander.

ctx.x: That's right. And what's your name?

My name, you want my full name? I don't like to use a full name, you know. But we already got it once. You already got it once. We can just use your short name. My short name, Paul Barberin. Okay. My full name happens to be Adolph Paul Barberin. Adolph Paul Barberin. That's your first name. That's my first name, yeah. I never liked that name because of the county name. It's antique, ancient. Who were you named after? Ah, now let's see. I must have written the name after my father's friend, Adolph Alexander. I…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: Oh, Adolph? Yeah. Adolph Alexander? Sure, he'll play.

ctx.x: Do you think you could get one that was in the class of the Owen Wood band? Oh, I think I could. Do you find a baritone player? Yeah, I'll find one right next to Nick's block. Can he still play?
Oh, Adolph? Yeah. Adolph Alexander? Sure, he'll play. I stroked in there in that pad, huh? Sure, he's all right now. Yeah.
I wonder if he had his lip back and all that. Huh?
